entries.254b61acf739aa32: This is the group's largest business, manufacturing and selling steel products. It is conducted by the operating company JFE Steel Corporation and its affiliates, which manufacture and sell various steel products, processed steel products and raw materials, among others, and also conduct peripheral businesses such as transportation and equipment maintenance and construction work. Main products and services are cold-rolled and surface-treated steel sheets, heavy plates, hot-rolled steel sheets, steel pipes, bars and wire rods, electrical steel sheets, shaped steel, stainless and specialty steel, iron powder, solutions and others. JFE Steel is a consolidated subsidiary in which the holding company holds 100.0% of voting rights; its main production sites are the East Japan Works (Chiba District and Keihin District), the West Japan Works (Kurashiki District and Fukuyama District), the Chita Works and the Sendai Works. Consolidated subsidiaries include JFE Bars & Shapes (shaped steel and rebar), JFE Chemical (chemical products) and JFE Logistics (transportation and warehousing), as well as an investment company for coal and iron ore mines in Australia, a sinter ore manufacturer in the Philippines, and hot-dip galvanized product manufacturers in Indonesia and Thailand; there are 103 other subsidiaries not listed in the table. Equity-method affiliates include Nihaku Niobium, an investment company in niobium mining in Brazil; Setouchi Kyodo Karyoku, a thermal power company; and JSW Steel Limited in India, among others. Following the acquisition of shares on March 30, 2026, JSW Kalinga Steel Limited newly became an equity-method affiliate (joint venture) of JFE Steel, and on April 17, 2026 it changed its name to JSW JFE Kalinga Steel Limited. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥2,756,616 million (¥3,007,924 million in the previous fiscal year), the largest of the three reportable segments. Revenue including intersegment transactions decreased 8.2% year on year due to lower steel prices, reduced sales volume and other factors. Consolidated crude steel production was 22.55 million tons, a decrease from the previous year. The number of employees as of March 31, 2026 was 41,654. The management policy describes a plan to streamline current crude steel production capacity of 26 million tons (a 7-blast-furnace system, excluding the electric furnace at the Sendai Works) to about 21 million tons in fiscal 2027 through blast furnace shutdowns. In fiscal 2028, an innovative electric furnace is to start operating at the West Japan Works (Kurashiki District), creating a system of 5 blast furnaces and 1 innovative electric furnace.

entries.3e0aba690b1ecf1c: This business builds and operates facilities such as plants and bridges, handling everything through to operation. JFE Engineering Corporation, an operating company, and its affiliates are responsible for it, conducting the engineering business in steel structures, industrial machinery, energy, environment and related fields, the recycling business and the electricity retail business. The main products and services are bridges and steel structures, industrial and machinery systems, offshore wind power, energy plants, pipelines, electricity business, environmental plants, recycling, water and sewerage systems and others. JFE Engineering is a consolidated subsidiary in which the holding company holds 100.0% of the voting rights. Its consolidated subsidiaries include JFE Plant Technology, which handles chemical and semiconductor-related plants; J&T Environment, which runs a comprehensive recycling business; JFE Project One, which handles petroleum refining and energy-related plants; and Urban Energy, which runs the electricity retail business. In Germany, it has Standard Kessel Baumgarten Holding GmbH, which builds plants for waste-to-energy and biomass power generation, and it has 78 other subsidiaries not named in the table. Its main manufacturing bases are Kasaoka Monopile Works (Kasaoka City, Okayama Prefecture), Tsu Works (Tsu City, Mie Prefecture) and Tsurumi Works (Tsurumi Ward, Yokohama City). In December 2025, it received its first order for monopiles for offshore wind power generation projects off Oga City, Katagami City and Akita City in Akita Prefecture, and in February 2026 it began manufacturing them at Kasaoka Monopile Works. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥583,657 million (¥554,156 million in the previous fiscal year), the third-largest of the three reportable segments. Revenue including intersegment transactions increased 5.3% year on year, as steady execution of orders received and corporate acquisitions led to a record high. Orders received grew, mainly due to an increase in construction and operation projects for waste treatment facilities. Number of employees as of March 31, 2026 was 11,170.

entries.66b4d2548340d2e9: This business purchases steel products and iron-making raw materials, processes them, and sells them. JFE Shoji Co., Ltd., an operating company, and its affiliates are responsible for it, purchasing, processing and selling steel products, iron-making raw materials, non-ferrous metal products, food products and others. The main products and services it handles are steel products (steel sheets, steel pipes, steel bars, wire rods, electrical steel sheets, shapes, stainless steel and special steel, iron powder and others), bridges and steel structures, industrial and machinery systems, offshore wind power, iron-making raw materials and environmental resources, equipment and materials, building materials, electronics, food products and others. JFE Shoji is a consolidated subsidiary in which the holding company holds 100.0% of the voting rights. Its consolidated subsidiaries include JFE Shoji Steel & Building Materials, which sells building materials products; JFE Shoji Electronics, which sells semiconductor products and others; Kawasho Foods, which trades in food products; and JFE Shoji Electrical Steel, which processes and sells electrical steel sheets. Overseas, it has steel sheet processing and sales companies and export-import trading companies in China, Indonesia, the United States, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Hong Kong and Canada, and it has 83 other subsidiaries not named in the table. Three consolidated subsidiaries of the steel business and one affiliate accounted for by the equity method are accounted for by the equity method in the trading business. Its management policy states that, in strategic collaboration with JFE Steel, it is developing a global steel supply chain management in Japan, China, North America, Australia, India and Europe. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,198,996 million (¥1,297,566 million in the previous fiscal year), making it the second-largest business among the reportable segments. Revenue including intersegment transactions decreased 7.3% year on year, as steel trading declined due to sluggish domestic construction demand and the effects of trade policies in various countries, and falling market conditions in Japan and overseas also contributed. Number of employees as of March 31, 2026 was 8,744.

entries.782f31bece3fe520: In May 2025 the company formulated “JFE Vision 2035” and its 8th Medium-term Management Plan (fiscal 2025 to 2027), and says it aims to complete them. In the Steel Business, the plan is to reduce crude steel production capacity from 26 million tons (7 blast furnaces; excluding the electric arc furnace at the Sendai Works) to around 21 million tons in fiscal 2027 through blast furnace shutdowns, and in fiscal 2028 to operate an innovative electric arc furnace at the Kurashiki area, for a structure of 5 blast furnaces and 1 innovative electric arc furnace. The company also cites expanding sales of high-value-added products, such as high-performance electrical steel sheet and high-tensile steel for automobiles, and expanding business in overseas growth regions, including an integrated steelworks joint venture with JSW Steel in India. In the Engineering Business, it received its first order for monopiles for offshore wind power projects in December 2025, and began manufacturing at the Kasaoka Monopile Works in February 2026. These include outlooks and plans as of the earnings announcement on May 8, 2026.
